observations: In media/state-03.png the active lock timeout is marked by a "✓" glyph beside the word "Immediately" and all nine choices are spelled out as text ("Immediately", "1 minute", "5 minutes", "15 minutes", "30 minutes", "1 hour", "4 hours", "On App Restart", "Never"), so the current setting is readable without colour.
That "✓ Immediately" row measures 4.05:1 in the retained frame: darkest pixel #58769b against lightest #e6f0f5 in the crop 158,101 58x12 of media/state-03.png.

The sheet's dismiss affordance is a separate white "Cancel" bar and it is the highest-contrast text on that screen at 4.33:1, darkest #597d9e against lightest #ffffff in the crop 150,315 70x14 of media/state-03.png.

Bitwarden's Settings screen at 101.10s of media/motion.mp4 prints each security value as a word at the right of its own row — "Lock Options / Immediately", "Unlock with Face ID / Enabled", "Unlock with PIN Code / Disabled" — instead of as a switch, so those states can be read from one still.

In media/state-02.png the tab bar carries a text label under every icon ("My Vault", "Generator", "Settings") and each vault row carries a numeric count beside its text label, so an empty category reads as "Card 0" and "Identity 0" rather than as icon shape alone; the "Login" label there measures 5.23:1, darkest #23283c against lightest #959ab0 in the crop 125,73 40x11.
unknowns: VoiceOver names, hints, rotor order, and focus return were not exposed by the source recording.
Dynamic Type behavior and text truncation at accessibility sizes were not exposed.
Reduce Motion behavior and a nonanimated equivalent were not exposed.
Switch Control, keyboard navigation, and haptic/audio-only feedback were not measured.
The phone is a 640x360 mockup inside a slide, so the contrast figures above come from that downscaled render and not from glyphs rasterized on a device.
No touch point, ripple, or focus ring is ever drawn inside the mockup, so which row was pressed is identified from the sheet's own "Lock Options" header rather than from a visible tap.

motion_analysis.trigger: The "Lock Options" row under Bitwarden's "SECURITY" heading, right-hand value "Immediately", is activated inside the phone mockup and the iOS action sheet headed "Lock Options" slides up from the bottom edge of the screen (media/motion.mp4 101.30s to 101.57s).
motion_analysis.start_state: Bitwarden "Settings" with no overlay: "AUTO-FILL" (Password AutoFill, App Extension), "MANAGE" (Folders, Sync 5/1/2020 11:26 AM), "SECURITY" (Lock Options — Immediately, Unlock with Face ID — Enabled, Unlock with PIN Code — Disabled, Lock Now, Two-step Login) and "ACCOUNT" (Change Master Password, Fingerprint Phrase); last clean frame 101.300s.
motion_analysis.end_state: The "Lock Options" action sheet settled at its resting height over the Settings list, "✓ Immediately" first, then "1 minute" through "Never", with a detached white "Cancel" bar below it (101.533s; the retained media/state-03.png is this state at 102.0s).
motion_analysis.continuity: The asset is a cut-edited tutorial reel — the right-hand caption panel hard-cuts from "Unlock with Face ID" to "Verify Face ID" between 97.00s and 97.25s while the left-hand phone mockup keeps running. Inside the mockup the one real product transition is unbroken: consecutive 30 fps frames at 101.300s, 101.333s, 101.400s, 101.467s and 101.533s show the sheet climbing from the bottom edge to its resting height with the Settings rows still visible behind it, with no cut. Transcoding to H.264 changed encoding only; no frames were synthesized.
motion_analysis.interruption_or_reversal: The same sheet is dismissed with no choice taken: it is still fully open at 103.967s, slides back down through 104.033s, 104.100s and 104.167s, and is gone at 104.200s, and the "Lock Options" row underneath still reads "Immediately" — the value it carried before the sheet opened.
motion_analysis.feedback: The overlay is itself the acknowledgment: it enters from the edge the finger came from, dims nothing but covers the list from the bottom up so the rows behind stay legible, and it restates the value already printed on the Settings row by putting a "✓" against "Immediately" (101.333s to 101.533s). The "Cancel" bar arrives last, separated from the option list by a gap.
